'''Ron Folman''' ({{langx|he|רון פולמן}}; born 16 February 1963), is an Israeli quantum physicist and [[social activist]]. He works at the [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]] (BGU) where he heads the Atom Chip group.<ref>{{cite web |title=Meet the group head - Ron Folman |url=http://www.bgu.ac.il/atomchip/ |website=bgu}}</ref> He is the author of the book ''The Human Test''.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Human Test |url=https://www.overdrive.com/media/11450011/the-human-test |website=overdrive}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=The Human Test: How Predictability, Creativity, and the Quantum Mind Will Redefine Life in the Age of AI |isbn=1-4930-8920-X }}</ref>

==Biography==

Folman, born in [[Tel Aviv]], is the son of Russian born Ahuva (Luba) Gordon and Polish born Yeshayahu Folman. Folman's mother, who barely escaped with her family from the burning city of Minsk as the Nazi army advanced, tried to make it to the land of Israel on the famous [[SS Exodus|Exodus refugee ship]], only to be returned by the British to [[Germany]].<br />
 
In 1998, Folman received his PhD degree<ref>{{Cite book |last=Folman |first=Ron |url=https://weizmann.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/permalink/972WIS_INST/10fp4af/alma990001467490203596 |title=Search for the Higgs boson with the OPAL detector at LEP at [radical symbol]s=161-172 GeV |publisher=Weizmann Institute of Science |year=1997}}</ref> from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] (work conducted at CERN).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ron Folman INSPIRE author profile |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1009744 |access-date=2024-02-26 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> Between 2000 and 2003, he worked as a researcher at the [[University of Heidelberg]] (Marie Curie fellow), Germany, and before that in 1999-2000 as a postdoctoral fellow in Innsbruck.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ron Folman |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3449-2563 |website=orcid}}</ref>
He is an advocate of [[Human Rights]], Animal Rights, Social justice, Peace and [[Environmental sustainability]].

Folman's father is a survivor of [[Auschwitz]] where he was numbered B-1367. Folman [[tattoo]]ed an exact replica on his arm.<ref>{{cite web |title=Auschwitz Concentration Camp Tattoo Shared by Father and Son |url=https://soundcloud.com/theworld/auschwitz-concentration-camp |website=soundcloud}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Son gets Dad's Auschwitz tattoo on own arm |url=http://www.bgu.ac.il/atomchip/People/Ron_Folman/Son%20gets%20Dad's%20Auschwitz%20tattoo%20on%20own%20arm%20-%20Haaretz%20-%20Israel%20News.pdf |website=bgu |publisher=Yair Ettinger}}</ref>

== Activism ==
[[File:Ron Folman presenting the Amensty International annual report on Human Rights.jpg|thumb|Ron Folman, Chairperson of Amnesty International, Israel Section, is presenting the Amnesty International annual report on Human Rights, to Shevah Weiss, Speaker of the Knesset (Israeli Parliament), Jerusalem, June 1994]]
* Human Rights: Folman has been a member of [[Amnesty International]] (AI) and in the 90s he was the chairperson of the Israeli Section of the organization. 
* Environmental Sustainability: Folman has been an active member of [[Greenpeace]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Activism |url=https://www.bgu.ac.il/atomchip/People/Activism.htm |website=bgu}}</ref>
* Social Justice: Folman was a member of the board of the university center for the promotion of [[education]] and careers among the [[Bedouins]] of the Negev desert.

==Science==
Folman<ref>{{cite web |title=PROF. RON FOLMAN |url=https://www.bgu.ac.il/atomchip/People/Ron_Folman/CV_Ron%20Folman_short_2020.pdf |website=Ben-Gurion University of the Negev}}</ref> is a [[professor]] of [[quantum physics]]<ref>{{cite book |title=Stern-Gerlach Interferometry with the Atom Chip |publisher=Mark Keil|arxiv=2009.08112 |last1=Keil |first1=Mark |last2=Machluf |first2=Shimon |last3=Margalit |first3=Yair |last4=Zhou |first4=Zhifan |last5=Amit |first5=Omer |last6=Dobkowski |first6=Or |last7=Japha |first7=Yonathan |last8=Moukouri |first8=Samuel |last9=Rohrlich |first9=Daniel |last10=Binstock |first10=Zina |last11=Bar-Haim |first11=Yaniv |last12=Givon |first12=Menachem |last13=Groswasser |first13=David |last14=Meir |first14=Yigal |last15=Folman |first15=Ron |year=2021 |pages=263–301 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-63963-1_14 |bibcode=2021mbpc.book..263K |isbn=978-3-030-63962-4 |s2cid=221761531 }}</ref> at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU) where he heads the Atom Chip group. He was the founder and first director of the BGU center for quantum science and technology since 2010,<ref>{{cite web |title=BGU center for quantum science and technology |url=https://in.bgu.ac.il/en/QI/Pages/default.aspx |website=bgu }}</ref> and the founder and first director of the center for nano-fabrication<ref>{{cite web |title=Nano-Fabrication center at Ben-Gurion university |url=https://in.bgu.ac.il/en/nano-fab/Pages/about.aspx |website=Ben-Gurion university}}</ref> since 2003. Folman is one of the [[inventor]]s of the Atom Chip.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fifteen Years of Cold Matter on the Atom Chip: Promise, Realizations, and Prospects |url=https://www.bgu.ac.il/atomchip/Papers/FifteenYears2016.pdf |website=bgu}}</ref> and is credited as realizing the first complete Stern-Gerlach interferometer.<ref>{{cite web |title=The (Often) Overlooked Experiment That Revealed the Quantum World |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/the-often-overlooked-experiment-that-revealed-the-quantum-world-20231205/ |website=quantamagazine |date=5 December 2023 |publisher=Zack Savitsky}}</ref> Folman is active in probing the interface between the general theory of relativity (gravity) and quantum mechanics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Scientists observe Einstein’s gravity in the quantum world |url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2026-08-28-scientists-observe-einsteins-gravity-in-the-quantum-world |website=University of Oxford |date=3 September 2026 |access-date=11 October 2026}}</ref> Folman is also involved in the search for new physics such as searches for [[Dark Matter]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Atomic probe of dark matter differential interactions with subatomic particles |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.015015 |journal=Physical Review D|date=2024 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.110.015015 |last1=Rosenzweig |first1=Yossi |last2=Kats |first2=Yevgeny |last3=Givon |first3=Menachem |last4=Japha |first4=Yonathan |last5=Folman |first5=Ron |volume=110 |issue=1 |article-number=015015 |arxiv=2312.05894 |bibcode=2024PhRvD.110a5015R }}</ref>
In 2011, he received the Willis Lamb award<ref>{{cite web |title=The 2011 Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics |url=http://www.lambmedal.org/2011/2011-folman.html |website=lambmedal}}</ref> and in 2013, he was a Miller [[visiting professor]] at Berkeley.<ref>{{cite web |title=Research explores magnetic fields of superconducting materials |url=https://www.dailycal.org/2014/03/18/research-explores-magnetic-fields-superconducting-materials/ |website=dailycal |date=18 March 2014 |publisher=ROBIN SIMMONDS}}</ref>

In 2021, Folman received the Falling Walls award for physics,<ref>{{cite web |title=THE SCIENCE BREAKTHROUGHS OF THE YEAR: FALLING WALLS ANNOUNCES SHORTLIST |url=https://falling-walls.com/press-releases/the-science-breakthroughs-of-the-year-falling-walls-announces-shortlist/ |website=falling-walls |access-date=2021-12-07 |archive-date=2021-12-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206164250/https://falling-walls.com/press-releases/the-science-breakthroughs-of-the-year-falling-walls-announces-shortlist/ }}</ref> and in 2023 was one of 11 worldwide to receive an award for an experiment that could transform our understanding of the universe.<ref>{{cite web |title=Together, math and science foundations fund tabletop physics that could transform our understanding of the Universe |url=https://www.moore.org/article-detail?newsUrlName=together-math-and-science-foundations-fund-tabletop-physics-that-could-transform-our-understanding-of-the-universe |website=moore}}</ref>
